hypothesis: THP on top of the PGO champion (THP has never been tested on Graviton5, and the earlier c8g "win" was host drift). 4.9% of light-phase samples were page faults, almost all in jemalloc arena growth, and each heavy call builds ~1 MB of storage maps; THP=always backs that anonymous memory with 2 MiB pages. Tests whether a system lever still stacks on top of a PGO build.
llm_commentary: THP=always on top of the PGO build is the round's second confirmed win and a new best: 4.31s [4.29/4.33/4.32] vs PGO's 4.43s [4.45/4.41/4.42], -2.7% with disjoint ranges, and -8.7% against the round's control (4.72s). Cost per run $0.000469. Notably this is a system lever stacking cleanly on a compiler lever: PGO improves code layout, THP cuts the page-walk cost of the heap that code touches, and they address different stalls. It also vindicates re-testing THP per CPU rather than trusting the earlier sweep: THP looked like a 3.9% win on Graviton4 but that turned out to be host drift, was neutral on x86, and had never been measured on Graviton5 at all. A PGO re-run without THP is in flight to bracket this delta the same way the PGO win was bracketed.
